tools.name: preview_schedule
tools.description: Find a valid schedule without saving anything. Up to six teams returns the full schedule. Larger leagues get a summary only. A capped search never returns an unproved repair.

tools.name: build_schedule
tools.description: Build a fair schedule, or repair original assignments after closed slots. Proves the fewest moved games. Free up to six teams. Above that, a season code is needed. It covers ten repairs, and the same request is not counted twice.

tools.name: check_schedule
tools.description: Check every game, field limit, coach conflict, home balance, blackout, weekly cap and rest rule. Returns violations and team counts. Free up to 70 teams.

tools.name: import_table
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 CSV, tab or semicolon table. Returns explicit rows. Quoted cells and blank lines are supported. Unknown columns are refused.

tools.name: export_schedule
tools.description: Return a base64 ZIP with team PDFs, field PDFs, team iCal files, schedule CSV and a moved games notice. Only checked full schedules are exported. Paid access is needed above six teams.

tools.name: publish_calendars
tools.description: Store checked calendar files for up to 366 days. Returns private feed links and a private owner key. An update with feedId and ownerKey keeps the same links. Anyone with a link can read its calendar.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "preview_schedule" appears informational but accepts parameters (code) that enable code/file/secret access.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "publish_calendars" appears informational but accepts parameters (code) that enable code/file/secret access.

evidence.snippet: season, schedule, code, feedId, ownerKey, closedSlotIds

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: publish_calendars · Private data: export_schedule, publish_calendars · Public sink: publish_calendars.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: publish_calendars · Private data: export_schedule, publish_calendars · Public sink: publish_calendars

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
